transportation.notes: Rickshaws are common for short trips

weather_info.climate_type: Semi-arid, continental climate with hot summers and cool winters
weather_info.best_time_to_visit: November to March (also ideal for citrus harvest season, December-February)

travel_tips.tip: Use the Sargodha Bypass to avoid the busy clock tower area when passing through toward Faisalabad or Lahore.
Rickshaws and local taxis are the most common way to get around; ride-hailing app coverage is more limited than in bigger cities.
Standard city precautions apply; Sargodha is generally a calm, agricultural city.
Visit during December-February if interested in the citrus orchards, which is peak harvest season for Sargodha's famous kinnow oranges.

history.founded: Developed significantly under British colonial canal-colony planning in the early 20th century
history.city_history: Sargodha grew rapidly after the British developed extensive irrigation canal networks in the region, turning it into one of Punjab's most productive agricultural areas, especially known for citrus fruit. It also has a long association with the Pakistan Air Force, hosting a major air base.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
